plain.li: Two of us had a fistfight over a chair this morning. It wasn't even a good chair.
Watch supper tonight. Two people will each wait for the other to leave before they sit down.
[winter] We'll be shut in together until the thaw. I'd rather not spend it listening to two people insult each other through a wall.

warm.li: Somebody cried in the storeroom yesterday where no one could see. It wasn't about the raids, it was about us.
[trait:Kind] I've been carrying apologies back and forth between two people for a week. I'd like them to just say it to each other.

blunt.li: Someone's been oversalting someone else's soup on purpose. Everyone knows who. Stop it.
[trait:Abrasive] I know I'm half the problem. I'm proposing it anyway. Fix the other half first.
[lowmood] I'm one snide remark away from throwing furniture, and I'm not even in the feud.

cheerful.li: We throw parties, one after another, until no one remembers what they were angry about!
[spring] Spring's for fresh starts! New crops, new leaves, and people saying good morning to each other again.

gloomy.li: When somebody snaps out here, it isn't a plate that gets broken. Let's settle this before then.
[grieving] I'd give anything for one more argument with the people we buried. You still have each other to argue with. Stop wasting it.

cold.li: Rivals don't cover each other in a fight. I've watched it happen, and it leaves a gap in our line.
[trait:Psychopath] I don't care who likes whom. I care that two of our best workers keep stopping to glare at each other.

plain.li: First supper in weeks where nobody took their plate outside to eat alone.
Somebody apologized at breakfast. Out loud, in front of people. I had to put my spoon down.

warm.li: I saw those two sharing a bench after supper tonight. They weren't talking, just sitting together.

blunt.li: Good. Whoever starts the next feud hauls corpses for a season.

cheerful.li: We all sat at one table tonight, and there weren't enough chairs!

gloomy.li: Everyone's getting along. I give it until the next long winter, but I'll enjoy it while it lasts.

cold.li: Nobody is wasting work hours on grudges anymore. I've kept a list, in case it starts again.

plain.li: There's a joke going around about this council, and it isn't a kind one.
[doubtful] We passed a decree last season. I watched people step around it like a puddle.
[newcomer] I'm new, so maybe I'm wrong. But when I ask people what the council is for, they shrug.

warm.li: Somebody asked for a shelf by their bed and we spent half a meeting arguing about the wood. Let's just give people the shelf.
[trusting] I still believe in this council. I'd like some company in that.

blunt.li: People stop listening to a council that doesn't listen to them.
[bitter] You promised me a lot of things. I've written them down. Start at the top.
[trait:Abrasive] People complain about the council to me because they think I'll be rude about it to your faces. I'm being rude about it to your faces.

cheerful.li: I want people lining up outside the meeting with requests, so many we need a queue!
[highmood] I'm in a fantastic mood and I'd like to spread it around! Let's start by keeping one promise and see how it feels.

gloomy.li: A colony that stops trusting its council starts trusting whoever shouts loudest. I've seen how that ends.
[lowmood] Every broken promise is a stone in somebody's pocket. Some of us are carrying a lot of stones.

cold.li: Granting a wish costs us once. A colonist who has stopped caring costs us every day.
[trait:Psychopath] People work harder when they believe someone's looking out for them. Whether we are is a separate question.

plain.li: Someone brought a complaint to the meeting today and actually expected an answer. That's new.
Somebody thanked the council today. Not sarcastically. I asked twice.

warm.li: People look up when we walk in now, instead of looking away. I hadn't noticed how much I missed that.

blunt.li: Took long enough. Don't make me pitch this again.

cheerful.li: Someone said "the council will sort it out" and meant it kindly! I heard it myself.

gloomy.li: They trust us now. That only means it'll hurt more when we let them down.

cold.li: Compliance is up, and nobody has noticed it's compliance. Good.

plain.li: Someone traded their good coat to a caravan for a pocketful of the stuff. We need to talk about that.
[afterraid] When the shooting started, somebody was still sleeping off last night's binge. We dragged them to cover by the collar.
[skill:Medicine] I've treated more overdoses this season than gunshot wounds. I'd rather go back to the gunshots.

warm.li: Withdrawal is miserable and lonely. If we do this, nobody goes through it by themselves. I'll sit up nights.
[trait:Ascetic] I don't need much, and I'm not asking anyone else to need nothing. Just not to need that.

blunt.li: Someone's been drinking the beer and topping the bottles up with water. I can taste it. Lock it all up.
Half the stockpile walks off at night in somebody's pockets. Lock it up and sit on the key.
[trait:Teetotaler] Half of you smell like a still at morning muster. I've been breathing through my mouth for a month.

cheerful.li: Think of the mornings! All of us up with the sun and clear-eyed, with no one sneaking behind the woodpile for a smoke.
[trait:ChemicalInterest] I know how this sounds coming from me. I'm proposing it anyway, so somebody hide everything from me first!

gloomy.li: I've seen people start a binge in the evening and never come out the other side. Everyone thinks it'll be someone else.
[lowmood] Some days the only thing that gets me through is the thing I'm proposing we take away. That's how I know we have to.

cold.li: Every dose we swallow is a dose we can't sell, and every addict works half the hours with twice the complaints.
[trait:Psychopath] Addicts are predictable in the worst way. They'll trade anything we own for the next dose, including each other.

plain.li: Took the lock off the medicine shelf today, and nothing went missing.
I checked behind the storeroom tonight and found nothing but rats.

warm.li: Somebody slept the whole night through, after a season of bad nights. I sat with them anyway, just in case.

blunt.li: Congratulations. You're all boring now. It's an improvement.

cheerful.li: Everybody's clean! I'm so proud I could drink a whole barrel of water.

gloomy.li: Clean. They say the cravings come back on bad days. We have a lot of bad days.

cold.li: No dependencies left. Our productivity no longer relies on a trader's inventory.

plain.li: They came over that ridge last time. I know which ridge. I know what's on the other side of it.
[hurt] I'm still stitched up from their last visit. I can walk. I can walk as far as their door.
[winter] The snow slows them down as much as us, and they'll be huddled around their fires. Let's go find the fires.

warm.li: [trait:Kind] I've never wanted to hurt anyone. I want even less to bury anyone else. Those are the only two choices they've left me.
[grieving] I keep saving a seat at supper out of habit. I'd like to stop. Maybe this lets me stop.

blunt.li: They know where we sleep. Time they learned we know where they sleep.
[trait:Pyromaniac] I'll carry the fuel. All of it. Nobody else touches the fuel.
[lowtech] Spears, bows, and a lot of angry people walking very quietly through the trees. That's the plan. Questions?

cheerful.li: We'll get back everything they stole, plus interest! I'm thinking their chairs.
[highmood] I know I'm smiling, but I'm also very angry, and you can be both. Let's go!

gloomy.li: No one comes home from something like this unchanged. I'll go anyway.
[afterraid] They'll come back no matter what we do. At least this way they'll have to rebuild first.

cold.li: [afterraid] Their losses yesterday mean their walls are thin today. In a week they won't be. Decide quickly.
[trait:Bloodlust] I enjoy this sort of thing. I'm telling you so you'll put me at the front, where it's useful.

plain.li: The smoke's still rising where their walls were. You can see it from the ridge if you want to. I don't.
We know the way there now. Anyone thinking of raiding us should keep that in mind.

warm.li: I counted heads the whole way back, over and over. Let's never have to do that again.

blunt.li: They had a lot of nice things. We have them now.

cheerful.li: We're back! Wash up, all of you, there's soot everywhere.

gloomy.li: I keep smelling smoke on my hands. I've washed them six times.

cold.li: Their stores were modest. The quiet from that direction is the real profit.

plain.li: Somebody's offering good silver for us to put up a few strangers for a while. We have the beds. Mostly.
[lowtech] A runner came through with word of someone who needs help, and a reward at the end of it. We should go and see.
[poor] We're scraping the bottom of every barrel we own. People out there are offering to fill a few. Let's say yes.

warm.li: There's a traveler stranded out there, waiting for help. I'd like it to be us who answers.
[trait:Kind] Every time we ignore a call for help, I lie awake wondering if anyone came. Let's be the ones who came.

blunt.li: Somebody wants to pay us to clear out a ruin. We'd have done that for free. Don't tell them.
[large] We've got more mouths than chores. Send a few of the mouths out to earn their dinner.
[trait:Greedy] They pay in silver. Heaps of it. I've done the sums, and I'd like to keep doing them.

cheerful.li: Imagine strangers around a campfire somewhere, telling stories about us! Probably the wrong stories, but still.
[spring] The snow's gone and the paths are open, and someone out there needs a few heroes!

gloomy.li: Nobody remembers the colonies that kept their heads down. They just stop being there one day.
[lowmood] Maybe if we're useful to someone out there, they'll come when it's our turn to need help. Maybe.

cold.li: Every favor we do is a debt someone else carries. I'd like a great many people owing us.
[trait:Psychopath] Grateful strangers are easy to recruit. If they don't work out, there are other options.

plain.li: A trader asked if we were the ones who helped with that business up north. I said yes. Felt good to say.
Came back with silver, a story and a limp.

warm.li: The people we helped sent word they're doing fine. That's the reward I'll remember.

blunt.li: Fine, we're heroes. Heroes still have to clean the kitchen.

cheerful.li: A caravan guard called me by name! I waved back much too hard.

gloomy.li: Now people out there know where to find us. That cuts both ways.

cold.li: Several factions now think well of us. I've made a note of which ones to test that on.
